content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving itraconazole, described in a fragmented and encoded format. 1. Itraconazole and Roflumilast: Itraconazole increases the plasma levels and effects of roflumilast by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring is required. Exercise caution when co-administering these drugs. 2. Itraconazole and Romidepsin: Itraconazole elevates the levels and effects of romidepsin through CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Itraconazole and Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates as clinically indicated. Close monitoring is advised. 4. Itraconazole and Rufinamide: Rufinamide decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain, but monitoring is recommended. 5. Itraconazole and Ruxolitinib: Itraconazole significantly increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg twice daily if platelet counts are ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use if platelet counts are <100 x 10^9/L. Alternative therapies are preferred. 6. Itraconazole and Saccharomyces boulardii: Itraconazole reduces the efficacy of Saccharomyces boulardii through an unspecified mechanism. Systemic or oral antifungals may decrease probiotic activity. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 7. Itraconazole and Salmeterol: Itraconazole increases salmeterol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, heightening the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 8. Itraconazole and Saxagliptin: Itraconazole raises saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Limit saxagliptin to 5 mg/day when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 9. Itraconazole and Seladelpar: Itraconazole increases seladelpar levels through CYP3A4 inhibition and other mechanisms. Monitor for adverse effects, especially when co-administered with BCRP inhibitors. 10. Itraconazole and Selpercatinib: Itraconazole elevates selpercatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 11. Itraconazole and Selumetinib: Itraconazole increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose as per its prescribing information. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 12. Itraconazole and Sertraline: Both itraconazole and sertraline prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 13. Itraconazole and Sevoflurane: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 14. Itraconazole and Sildenafil: Itraconazole raises sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Sildenafil is not recommended during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment when used for pulmonary arterial hypertension. 15. Itraconazole and Silodosin: Itraconazole increases silodosin levels through CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Itraconazole and Simvastatin: Itraconazole significantly increases simvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 17. Itraconazole and Siponimod: Itraconazole elevates siponimod levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 18. Itraconazole and Sirolimus: Itraconazole increases sirolimus levels through CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 19. Itraconazole and Sodium Bicarbonate: Sodium bicarbonate reduces itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH, affecting its absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 20. Itraconazole and Sodium Citrate/Citric Acid: Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 21. Itraconazole and Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate reduces itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer drugs with pH-dependent solubility at least two hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Monitor closely. 22. Itraconazole and Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Itraconazole increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Itraconazole and Solifenacin: Itraconazole raises solifenacin levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Itraconazole and Sonidegib: Itraconazole increases sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 25. Itraconazole and Sorafenib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 26. Itraconazole and Sotalol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 27. Itraconazole and Sparsentan: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. 28. Itraconazole and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Itraconazole and Stiripentol: Stiripentol affects itraconazole metabolism as a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for altered effects. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 30. Itraconazole and Sufentanil: Itraconazole increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially leading to prolonged adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 31. Itraconazole and Sulfamethoxazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 32. Itraconazole and Sunitinib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 33. Itraconazole and Suvorexant: Itraconazole increases suvorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Itraconazole and Tacrolimus: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 35. Itraconazole and Tadalafil: Itraconazole increases tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid concurrent use for pulmonary hypertension. Adjust tadalafil dosage for other indications. 36. Itraconazole and Talazoparib: Itraconazole increases talazoparib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 37. Itraconazole and Tamoxifen: Itraconazole increases tamoxifen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4, reducing its metabolism to active metabolites. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 38. Itraconazole and Tamsulosin: Itraconazole increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is not recommended during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 39. Itraconazole and Tasimelteon: Itraconazole increases tasimelteon levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Itraconazole and Tazemetostat: Itraconazole increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 41. Itraconazole and Tecovirimat: Tecovirimat decreases itraconazole levels as a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness. 42. Itraconazole and Telavancin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Itraconazole and Temsirolimus: Itraconazole increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 44. Itraconazole and Teniposide: Itraconazole increases teniposide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Itraconazole and Terbinafine: Itraconazole increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Itraconazole and Tetrabenazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 47. Itraconazole and Tezacaftor: Itraconazole increases tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 48. Itraconazole and Theophylline: Itraconazole increases theophylline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 49. Itraconazole and Thioridazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 50. Itraconazole and Ticagrelor: Itraconazole increases ticagrelor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 51. Itraconazole and Tipranavir: Itraconazole increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 52. Itraconazole and Tisotumab Vedotin: Itraconazole increases tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Monitor for increased systemic exposure and adverse effects. 53. Itraconazole and Tobramycin (Inhaled): Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to reduce ototoxicity risk. 54. Itraconazole and Tofacitinib: Itraconazole increases tofacitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 55. Itraconazole and Tolterodine: Itraconazole increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 56. Itraconazole and Tolvaptan: Itraconazole significantly increases tolvaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated.
